note: One Fish Audio library voice per NPC for the [NPC: Name] tag (discord-voice-bridge src/npcvoices.js). Entry: {name, aliases[], floors[], fish_voice_id (32 hex or null = narrator voice), note}; optional npc_id, type, voice_cue, fish_voice_name. Written by `npm run npc-voices:import -- <sheet.xlsx|.csv>`; the bridge reloads it on change. GM Narrator and The System stay on FISH_VOICE_ID_NARRATOR / FISH_VOICE_ID_SYSTEM.

npcs.name: The Audience
npcs.note: The unseen viewers, heard as laugh tracks, gasps, boos and wolf-whistles.
npcs.voice_cue: Crowd reactions only (laughs, gasps, boos); Silent/non-verbal - optional

npcs.name: Benefactor
npcs.note: A mystery patron heard only as faint private static ("...HOLD... NOT YET...") by a dying Crawler; becomes a real offer later.
npcs.voice_cue: Very far away, very tired; whispery, broken by static

npcs.name: Bruiser the Mascot
npcs.note: An empty 8-ft pit-bull mascot costume that animates and fights in the Locker Room; nobody is inside.
npcs.voice_cue: Silent/non-verbal - optional

npcs.name: Dale Pruitt
npcs.note: Kind 50s HVAC tech caught in a trap net; rescue target and tag-along who knows buildings. F2 only mentions him (escort board / permanence scrap).
npcs.voice_cue: Wheezy, friendly middle-aged everyman; nervous, chatty about ductwork

npcs.name: Dean Thudd
npcs.note: Head of Orientation, Floor 1 final boss: a huge ogre in a too-small mortarboard who counts down before his 'GROUP PHOTO' smash; can be talked into retiring. F2 only has callbacks (alumni ads).
npcs.voice_cue: Booming, dim, proud high-school principal; big jock energy, weepy when moved

npcs.name: Dean Thudd (JV)
npcs.note: Smaller bugbear version of Dean Thudd used for level-1 or 2-Crawler parties; same gown, bigger chip on his shoulder.
npcs.voice_cue: Like Dean Thudd but smaller and whinier; insecure, trying too hard

npcs.name: Exit Greeter
npcs.note: Goblin Orientation staff in a green vest with a clipboard guarding the fake EXIT; 'has a quota'.
npcs.voice_cue: Overly polite goblin receptionist; nasal, clipped customer-service voice

npcs.name: Exit Greeter (Trainee)
npcs.note: The junior goblin greeters with the leader at the fake EXIT; 'has a quota and a dream'.
npcs.voice_cue: Squeaky, eager young goblin intern; overexcited

npcs.name: Proctor Bell
npcs.note: Floor 1 trainer: a painted wooden fortune-teller automaton in a glass booth on ceiling rails; sells 1-credit hints. F2 is a GM callback / cracked booth only.
npcs.voice_cue: Music box with a head cold; clacking jaw, creaky, faux-cheerful, slightly menacing ("little lambs")

npcs.name: Pudding
npcs.note: Optional Assigned Companion for 2-Crawler tables: a mastiff in a tiny mortarboard who belongs to nobody.
npcs.voice_cue: Silent/non-verbal - optional (barks only)

npcs.name: Snakk-Matic
npcs.note: The cheerful vending terminal in the Break Room and Green Room; sells potions and an unlisted spare key; goes dark on Day 4.
npcs.voice_cue: Bright, upbeat commercial jingle voice; slightly shady salesman under it

npcs.name: Tanya Ruiz
npcs.note: A crawler who died before the party arrived; her lore-scrap note is the only way she 'speaks'.
npcs.voice_cue: Tired, scared young woman in scrubs; shaky, trying to be brave (optional: only if her note is read aloud)

npcs.name: Bazaar Vendor
npcs.note: Generic Rec-Hall Bazaar stall vendor with limited stock (the F2 'named district vendors' are not named yet); a static sigil hides behind one stall.
npcs.voice_cue: Smiling street hawker; 'smiles like a trap'

npcs.name: Cascadia
npcs.note: The show's floor announcer on Floor 2; cheerful corporate notices padding bad news, stern only about bathrooms. Her notices currently play in the System voice.
npcs.voice_cue: Falsely chipper store-manager woman; salesy, condescending, secretly burnt out

npcs.name: Guide
npcs.note: Cheerful Floor 2 guide offering a 'free route map' with unread fine print (Guide Contract); the debt bites on F4 and is called on F9.
npcs.voice_cue: Smiling, too-friendly timeshare salesman; smooth, fast talker

npcs.name: Krakaren Clone
npcs.note: Floor 2 Neighborhood Boss: a screaming tentacled octopus copy (not the original) that bursts out of its chamber; the twist is unmasking it.
npcs.voice_cue: Many screaming human mouths at once; wet, layered, unhinged

npcs.name: Laminak Rev-Up Consultant Elite
npcs.note: Leaf-suited sprite 'managers' above the clurichauns in the Rev-Up scheme; scream for their manager Damien when dying.
npcs.voice_cue: Shrill tiny upper-management sprite; corporate buzzwords, panicky

npcs.name: Meadow Lark Resident
npcs.note: Frail elderly residents in the Day 9 wheelchair convoy (individual names still to be written); one row for the group.
npcs.voice_cue: Elderly, frail, cranky-to-sweet grandparent voices

npcs.name: Mexx-55
npcs.note: Frisbee-shaped greeter robot with one blue light in the optional Death Watch studio trailer.
npcs.voice_cue: Soothing, flat female robot voice; calm, polite

npcs.name: Prince Maestro
npcs.note: Boar-like orc host of the optional Death Watch game show (pages call him 'the host'); cruel, egotistical, calls Crawlers meat.
npcs.voice_cue: Loud, bullying alien talk-show host; grunting, thin-skinned, tantrums

npcs.name: Qwist
npcs.note: Bopca Protector who runs the Big Shot Chicken saferoom: cooks, fusses over guests, sells pet biscuits at markup. The most-talked-to F2 NPC.
npcs.voice_cue: Fussy, motherly, clucky little caretaker; warm, worried, 'have you eaten?'

npcs.name: Rage Elemental
npcs.note: Avoidable punishment spawn summoned if a Crawler relieves themselves outside a bathroom or saferoom; likely kills everyone.
npcs.voice_cue: Silent/non-verbal - optional (roars)

npcs.name: Ralph the Frenzied Gerbil
npcs.note: Absurdly cute gerbil pit-fighter of the kobold dog pound whose mouth opens impossibly wide; survives being swallowed.
npcs.voice_cue: Non-verbal (squeaks, shrieks); Silent/non-verbal - optional

npcs.name: Unvaccinated Clurichaun Rev-Up Consultant
npcs.note: Sniffly goblin-like bottom-tier sellers in the Rev-Up moonshine pyramid scheme; their hits block healing.
npcs.voice_cue: Congested, sniffly MLM hustler; pushy pitch, Irish-ish drunk lilt

npcs.name: Zev
npcs.note: Show liaison/producer in a bubbling water helmet who reports the elderly-escort storyline is playing well.
npcs.voice_cue: Nervous, friendly young producer; bubbly, slightly gurgly

npcs.name: Hedge Appraiser
npcs.note: Village appraiser on Floor 3 who shrugs at the Odd Coin.
npcs.voice_cue: Unimpressed rural old-timer; slow, dry

npcs.name: Low Chapel Bishop
npcs.note: The village chapel's bishop on Floor 3 who turns up at court on Floor 9.
npcs.voice_cue: Soft-spoken clergyman who grows grand and political

npcs.name: Village Elder
npcs.note: Elder of the Floor 3 villages (Wellspring / Millroad / Low Chapel), the people Crawlers first meet.
npcs.voice_cue: Weathered, careful village elder; warm but wary

npcs.name: Village Saint
npcs.note: The harvest saint the Benefactor crest is mistaken for on F3; an icon on F9; sits on a throne of storms on F12.
npcs.voice_cue: Gentle folk-saint who becomes thunderous and divine

npcs.name: Customs Officer
npcs.note: Collects customs fees at the Floor 6 dock saferooms and customs houses.
npcs.voice_cue: Bored, stamp-happy bureaucrat

npcs.name: Dock Appraiser
npcs.note: Floor 6 dock appraiser who offers a number for the Odd Coin that is wrong on purpose.
npcs.voice_cue: Slick, sly harbor fence; low and smiling

npcs.name: Licensed Hunter
npcs.note: Licensed outsiders who hunt Crawlers from Floor 6; knights or outlaws on F9; possible named duel on F11.
npcs.voice_cue: Cocky professional hunter; calm, predatory

npcs.name: Sponsor
npcs.note: Rich patrons in skyboxes who shop for Crawlers and pets on F6, hold court seats on F9 and paid for an ending on F18.
npcs.voice_cue: Oily, wealthy, bored aristocrat; condescending

npcs.name: Echo Self
npcs.note: Memory echoes wearing a Crawler's face on Floor 8; mirror versions may climax on Floor 16.
npcs.voice_cue: Distorted, slightly-off copy of a Crawler's own voice

npcs.name: Chapel God
npcs.note: The Low Chapel's god, physically present on the Olympus floor.
npcs.voice_cue: Vast, resonant, ancient divine voice

npcs.name: Auditor
npcs.note: Debt-vault auditors on Floor 13 'who smile with no mouth'.
npcs.voice_cue: Cold, polite, whispery accountant; no breath

npcs.name: Auctioneer
npcs.note: Runs the Floor 14 reality-lot auction (implied by the lots and paddles; not named yet).
npcs.voice_cue: Rapid-fire auction chant; showman

npcs.name: Choir Boss
npcs.note: Infernal choir bosses of Floor 15 who hold damned contracts.
npcs.voice_cue: Layered hymn-scream; choral, demonic

npcs.name: Stagehand
npcs.note: Backstage crew under the broadcast grid on Floor 17 who know the exits Crawlers were never sold.
npcs.voice_cue: Gruff, whispering union crew; tired, conspiratorial

npcs.name: The Owners
npcs.note: The owner club at the Cage Bottom who run the Crawl, the final politics of Floor 18.
npcs.voice_cue: Smug, polished, ultra-rich; amused, quiet menace
